newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's ousted Bhutto happy at Clinton win.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's ousted Bhutto happy at Clinton win.

text.p: Pakistan's ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto on Wednesday greeted the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton, saying he was "the perfect person" to lead America into the 21st century.
There was no immediate comment on Clinton's victory from the caretaker government of Prime Minister Meraj Khalid.
President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto's three-year-old government on Tuesday, dissolved the National Assembly and named Khalid to supervise parliamentary elections set for February 3.

The anti-Bhutto Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party made no comment on Clinton's win, but welcomed the defeat of Republican Senator Larry Pressler, hated in Pakistan for sponsoring legislation that halted U.S. military aid to Islamabad.
"I am very happy that President Clinton has won," Bhutto said at her first news conference after her dismissal for alleged corruption and misrule. She denied the charges.
"He is a young and dynamic leader and I think he is the perfect person to guide America into the 21st century," she said.

"I feel a lot of empathy because I think we are both leaders of the new generation and I think we both... are against traditional modes. He doesn't have a wife who is traditional and I am not traditional because I am a woman, and I think that's why there is a smear campaign against him and his wife."

Bhutto's talks with Clinton last year led to the easing of a U.S. arms embargo against Pakistan imposed in 1990 under the so-called Pressler Amendment. The ban was a response to suspicions that Pakistan was trying to make nuclear weapons.
Bhutto, whose critics accused her of toeing an American line abroad, said she was not dependent on foreign support.
"I have been elected as prime minister, and I will be prime minister again, not because of any foreign power, not because of any institutional power, but because of...the people of Pakistan."
A U.S. State Department spokesman said on Tuesday that Leghari's sacking of Bhutto, using his discretionary powers, appeared to be constitutional.
A statement by PML information secretary Mushahid Hussain said Pressler's defeat by Senator Tim Johnson on Tuesday "should augur well for Pakistan".
He urged the Pakistani government to take "vigorous steps" to have the Pressler Amendment repealed because, he said, after Pressler's election defeat this law also stood discredited.
Pakistan, a threshold nuclear power, has refused to sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty or the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT) unless its arch-foe India does the same.
